claim: Classical logic's explosion is a design choice. Several families (LP, FDE/Belnap, C-systems/LFIs, discussive, relevant, adaptive) block it in different ways, so S6 can choose how far a contradiction may spread.
agent_test: Give the agent an inconsistent premise set. Compare policies (quarantine, mark-consistent, retract) on how many unrelated questions it still answers right at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: LP-style 'both' (glut) values and Belnap's four values let a record keep evidence for and against a claim separately instead of a single truth value; in Allen et al. (2025) a bilateral verify/refute judge raised macro-F1 by about 0.06 but lowered coverage by about 0.46, so it is not free.
agent_test: Memory entries carry (for, against) flags. Test whether contradictory notes are kept and flagged rather than overwritten.
audit_note: LP 'both' value and Belnap's four values are real, and Allen et al. use a bilateral (verify/refute) record, but no source calls this cheap: Allen et al. report macro-F1 +0.062 at a coverage cost of -0.456, and a14/b10 are the same paper.
claim_before_audit: LP-style 'both' (glut) values and Belnap's four values give a cheap bilateral record: store evidence-for and evidence-against separately instead of one truth value.

claim: Consistency-marked explosion (da Costa C-systems): explosion is restored only for claims marked consistent, so the agent can reason classically on trusted parts.
agent_test: Mark verified facts as consistent. Test whether derivations touching only marked facts stay classical and others stay contained.

claim: Adaptive logics reason classically by default and retract derived lines when an abnormality (A and not A) involving them appears.
agent_test: Retract-on-conflict operator: track which lines depend on conflicting premises. Measure accuracy after a late contradiction is injected.

claim: People accept some borderline contradictions: at the 5'11 midpoint 44.7% called 'tall and not tall' true and 53.9% called 'neither tall nor not tall' true (N=76, one study).
agent_test: Not an agent test. It only shows human reasoners tolerate glut-like states.

claim: Acceptance of glut sentences is fragile: Serchuk et al. (via Egre) found 'x is P and x is not P' true for 66/350 (19%) and 25/350 (7%); Egre et al. N=148 found 'and' far less accepted than 'neither' (coef -4.35) with order effects (about 50% to 35%) and adjective effects (about 37% to 66%).
agent_test: Not an agent test. Warns against treating human data as strong support for dialetheism.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: In Alxatib and Pelletier (2011), 53.7% (22 of 41) of those who judged 'neither tall nor not tall' true of the 5'11 man also judged 'tall and not tall' true, so gap and glut answers often come from the same people; Egre et al. report that 'neither' descriptions are nonetheless preferred to 'and' descriptions.
agent_test: Not testable on the agent.
audit_note: 53.7% (22 of 41) verified in Alxatib and Pelletier, but that means about half, not that gap and glut answers come from the same people; the Egre et al. 37% figure could not be opened (HAL blocked; abstract found says 'neither' is preferred to 'and', i.e. gaps over gluts); a11 and b02 are one paper.
claim_before_audit: Gap and glut answers come from the same people: 53.7% of 'neither' acceptors at 5'11 also accepted 'both'; over 37% accepted both in Egre et al.

claim: Pragmatic accounts (strict-tolerant, st-consequence) explain the borderline-contradiction data without dialetheism, while a reply argues they predict wrong interpretations.
agent_test: None.

claim: Bilateral (separate verify and refute) LLM judging raises macro-F1 by about 0.06 (GPQA flagship 0.699 vs 0.633; SimpleQA flagship 0.736 vs 0.657), but only on non-abstained items; coverage falls to about 0.50-0.59.
agent_test: Run verify-only vs verify+refute prompts on our own claim set. Report F1 and coverage at equal tokens, not only on answered items. Gap search d11: unilateral baseline had coverage 1.000, so the F1 gain is not matched on coverage; run a unilateral judge that abstains at the same 0.5-0.6 coverage.

claim: Bilateral judging costs about 2x time and tokens (GPQA flagship 4,782 vs 2,213 tokens; SimpleQA distilled 3,964 vs 2,167).
agent_test: Compare bilateral against unilateral with 2x samples (self-consistency) at equal tokens. The paper has no equal-cost comparison.

claim: LLM judges often return gluts: flagship models gave (true,true) on about 30% of claims. Families differ a lot (GPT glut 59%, gap near 0; Claude glut 19.6%, gap 30.4%).
agent_test: Treat a glut flag from the model as a cue to send the claim to external verification, not as a verdict.

claim: A symbolic reasoner over a medication knowledge base found 92 gluts in 940 statements while the theory stayed satisfiable.
agent_test: Keep a small KB of agent claims, detect gluts by rule, and see whether repairs improve final answers.

claim: Frontier LLMs often keep deducing from a contradictory premise set: GPT-4o halted correctly on 56.0% and Gemma-3-4B on 43.9% of 800 contradiction items. Example: given {A->B, A, not B}, GPT-4o concludes B.
agent_test: Inject contradictory premises into multi-step tasks. Measure halt, flag and blind-continue rates.

claim: Fine-tuning for contradiction halting reaches 1.000 on synthetic data, but 'correct' there means halt, not paraconsistent reasoning.
agent_test: Do not adopt. Our agent is not trained, and halting is not the goal at S6.

claim: LLMs rarely notice or report conflicting inputs unprompted. WikiContradict no-cue correct 2.1-10.4% (cue 10.4-43.8%); PCBench proactive critique 4.0-40.5% vs 53.5-77.9% when told to check.
agent_test: Add an explicit conflict-check line in S6 and measure the lift on conflicting-source QA at equal tokens.
audit_note: Minor: WikiContradict figures (2.1-10.4% no cue; 10.4-43.8% with cue) verified in PDF table, PCBench 4.0-40.5% and 53.5-77.9% verified in paper; WikiContradict measures answers that reflect both passages, not noticing as such.

claim: Conflict-aware prompting helps mainly on explicit conflicts (Llama-3-70b 13.3% to 60.0% explicit vs 5.9% to 17.6% implicit); GPT-4 gains little (6.3% to 10.4%).
agent_test: Split explicit and implicit conflicts in the agent test set.

claim: Knowing the conflict type helps but is hard: type prediction is 53-65% accurate; an oracle type adds about 24 points of adherence, a pipeline only 9.
agent_test: Test a conflict-type step before answering.

claim: Detecting self-contradiction in documents is hard: binary accuracy 50-54% for GPT-3.5, GPT-4, PaLM2, LLaMA2 (GPT-4 recall 8.0% at 97% precision). GPT-4 finds the evidence in its top-5 70.2% of the time.
agent_test: Use evidence localisation before the verdict. Test on long agent scratchpads.
audit_note: ContraDoc numbers verified in the paper (50.1/53.8/52.0/50.5%; GPT-4 recall 8.0% at 97% precision; top-5 evidence hit 70.2%); b17 and b18 are one paper.

claim: Missing or flawed premises make reasoning models overthink without reporting the flaw (cost ratio flawed vs normal up to 3.90 for o3-mini). R1 deliberated on the conflict, then silently used one side.
agent_test: Add a budget cap and a mandatory 'report the conflict' line at S6. Measure tokens and report rate.
audit_note: Minor: 3.90 is the o3-mini proactive cost ratio on the easy subset in PCBench Table 2; the R1 'deliberated then silently used one side' is a single case study, not a rate; Fan et al. say reasoning models are slow to recognise the missing premise rather than never doing so.

claim: Premise order changes accuracy by up to 20-30% for GPT-4-turbo and PaLM 2-L in deduction, so order effects can mask handling of inconsistency.
agent_test: Randomise premise order in all S6 tests.

claim: Solver-backed consistency checks with core-guided repair raise cross-query consistency (SetCons deep subset 0.52 to 0.91), but self-consistency K=20 reaches 0.88-0.94 without a solver at similar overhead (1.48-1.58x vs 1.51x).
agent_test: Compare a retract-on-core operator with plain self-consistency at equal tokens.

claim: Accuracy gains from consistency repair are small (R1 0.80 to 0.85; deep subset 0.77 to 0.81).
agent_test: Measure answer accuracy, not only consistency.

claim: Logic-enhancing pipelines can hurt where rules should be defeated: LogicLM and SymbolicCoT lowered paired accuracy on Rulebreakers; only one of 7 models exceeded 0.6 (chance 0.25).
agent_test: Do not add a rigid classical logic checker. Test any checker on defeasible items.

claim: Revising a belief after a minimal premise edit is hard for small models (Qwen3-1.7B initial 0.667, revised 0.467, inertia 0.600).
agent_test: Test edit-then-requery on our agent.

claim: No 2020-2026 study found that tests paraconsistent logic as a scaffold for LLM agents or tests explosion directly. Searches for 'Belnap four-valued LLM' and 'contradictory premises LLM explosion' returned zero hits. Gap-search re-run (d18): APIs were at HTTP 429 again and web search found only Allen et al. 2025; still weak evidence of absence.
agent_test: The gap itself: an equal-token test of paraconsistent S6 handling would be new.

claim: LLM conflict adjudication is order sensitive: reversing two contradictory documents flips the answer for 11.4-25.2% of items (mean 18.6%, accuracy gap 11.1 points, 920 paired predictions per model, six 4B-14B open models). Conflict detection in ECon changes less on the first dataset (about 0.4-1.8 F1 points for Claude 3 Sonnet, Llama-3 70B, GPT-4 and Llama-3 8B), but the paper says most detectors are order sensitive and larger drops appear in other columns of its Table 16.
agent_test: Run every S6 adjudication in both orders (or randomise); count answer flips as a conflict signal.
audit_note: Han et al. numbers (11.4-25.2%, mean 18.6%, gap 11.1, 920 per model, six 4B-14B models) verified; but the ECon '0.4-2.8 F1' comes only from the first dataset column of Table 16 and 2.8 is Mixtral, not a strong LLM (strong models there move 0.4-1.8); other columns of the table show drops of about 3-6 points.
claim_before_audit: LLM conflict adjudication is order sensitive: reversing two contradictory documents flips the answer for 11.4-25.2% of items (mean 18.6%, accuracy gap 11.1 points, N=920 per model, 6 small models). Detection of the conflict is much less order sensitive (ECon: 0.4-2.8 F1 points for strong LLMs).

claim: Conflict type changes detection a lot: self-contradiction inside one document is hardest (accuracy 0.006-0.456), cross-document pairs easiest (up to 0.893). Recall is low for all models while precision stays above 0.9.
agent_test: Add a dedicated self-consistency pass over the agent's own trace at S6 entry; do not rely on unprompted detection.
audit_note: Minor: Gokul et al. figures (0.006-0.456 self-contradiction, 0.893 pair, high precision/lower recall) verified in PDF text on a synthetic dataset; 'precision above 0.9' not individually checked per model; ECon (high precision, weaker-model low recall) only partly corroborates.

claim: Unprompted LLMs often silently choose a side in conflicts (ECon: 24% of Sonnet and 38% of Haiku responses resolve by chance; PCBench unprompted premise critique 4.0-40.5%). An explicit premise-check instruction raises reporting to 53.5-77.9% across PCBench models (R1 67.7%, Gemini-2.0-flash-thinking 77.9%) and for some reasoning models cuts tokens (R1 2590 to 1014; o3-mini 1279 to 1023 on the easy set).
agent_test: Make a one-line conflict register mandatory at S6 entry and measure reports and tokens against an unprompted baseline.
audit_note: ECon 24%/38% chance and PCBench R1/o3-mini token numbers and 4.0-40.5% unprompted range are correct, but instructed critique rates across PCBench models range 53.5-77.9%, not 67.7-77.9% (e.g. Qwen3-8B-thinking 57.2, Llama-4/others 53.5-61.8).
claim_before_audit: Unprompted LLMs silently choose a side in many conflicts (24% Sonnet, 38% Haiku resolve by chance in ECon; PCBench unprompted critique 4.0-40.5%). A forced premise check raises reporting to 67.7-77.9% and, for reasoning models, cuts tokens (R1 2590 to 1014; o3-mini 1279 to 1023).

claim: Listing every candidate answer with source-tied explanation before adjudicating (XoT) beats direct, CoT and conflict-aware prompts on text-vs-KG conflicts (GPT-4o about +20% relative F1; Open-Mistral-7B about 3x), but it was not compared with retraction or halting and not at equal tokens.
agent_test: Test keep-both-then-adjudicate against retract and halt at equal tokens on injected-contradiction tasks (gap 1).

claim: Bilateral judging's F1 gain over a unilateral judge is confounded with abstention: unilateral coverage was 1.000, bilateral 0.499-0.589. No matched-coverage or matched-token control exists in the literature I found.
agent_test: Run unilateral judge + confidence-based abstention at equal coverage and tokens; only then credit the bilateral structure.

claim: Revision after a premise edit fails mostly on support-removal and defeating-fact edits (Qwen3-1.7B 0.0 on both; Qwen3-4B 0.000 on support-removal) while support-insertion is easy; N is 20-30 episodes and no retraction method was tested.
agent_test: Build edit-then-requery tests split by edit type; compare dependency-tracked retraction vs full re-solve.

claim: Glut rates from LLM judges vary by model family (59.0% GPT, 19.6% Claude, 52.9% Llama) and topic (63.6% video games to 35.7% history), so a fixed glut threshold cannot be a universal trigger; a learned conflict score beats raw confidence for abstention (+33.4 points at 25% coverage).
agent_test: Calibrate glut and conflict trigger per model and per topic before using it to trigger tool verification.
